title: 12th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened with routine business: minutes adopted, committee membership change announced, an urgent matter declined and a bill on seeking public opinion given its first reading. MPs then finished debating the bill to amend the Judges Act (2010/13), with the sponsor's closing remarks, and began debating the State Owned Enterprises committee report on MMPRC and Maldives Integrated Tourism Development Corporation, which turned into a sharp exchange between government and opposition members. After a 30-minute break, the Judges Act amendment was accepted 69-0 and sent to the Judiciary Committee. Parts of the PDF text were garbled, so the attendance numbers are a best reading.

items.title: Announcement of attendance
items.outcome: 26 members present, 6 on leave, none on official travel at the start

items.title: Adoption of minutes of sittings 2025/2/6 to 2025/2/8
items.outcome: accepted as no amendments were submitted

items.title: Announcements by the chair: committee change, guests, urgent matter
items.outcome: Asma Rasheed named to the Human Rights and Gender Committee; urgent matter from the Vaikaradhoo member declined as it did not meet the rules

items.title: Bill on seeking public opinion and holding a public vote
items.outcome: first reading read, submitted by the Inguraidhoo member for the government

items.title: Debate on the bill to amend the Judges Act (Act 2010/13)
items.outcome: debated; sponsor closed the debate; vote held after the break (see item 9)

items.title: State Owned Enterprises committee report on MMPRC and Maldives Integrated Tourism Development Corporation (M20/R/SOE/2025/02)
items.outcome: presented and debated; debate not concluded in this part

items.title: Vote on accepting the Judges Act amendment bill
items.outcome: passed 69-0; sent to the Judiciary Committee

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Backed the Judges Act amendments, saying Feydhoo's court has operated from a house since it was burned and judges need protection.
Raised a point of order to correct a statement about GMR and the airport; the chair did not treat it as a point of order.
Said an earlier speaker's claims on the MMPRC case were inaccurate and urged parliamentary committees to examine such cases.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said judges need independence and protection, pointing to Singapore, and that the justice system must treat people equally.
Defended the SOE report, saying opposition claims on company losses overlook past governance and citing a 2023 Fenaka audit.
Raised a point of order saying he was not a thief and had not stolen from the state.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the bill, saying earlier governments interfered with the courts and the amendments bring protections and standards for judges.
Said the SOE report is sound, that companies were already insolvent in 2023, and described unfinished advance-paid projects.
Raised a point of order that accusing all PNC members of lying implied self-interest, asking for it to be clarified.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said he saw nothing in the bill that would speed up trials and that neither the judiciary nor the Majlis is independent.
On the SOE report, said parliament should question government priorities such as Rasmale reclamation rather than keep debating reports.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said three minutes is too short to debate such a report and that the debate had become blame between governments.
Said state companies post profits and called for housing and development promises to be met.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said the MMPRC case is a larger matter and called for those involved to face justice.
Criticised the handling of Hulhumale' Phase 2 plots and referred to money passing through Bank of Maldives to SOF.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Said justice delayed is justice denied and that reforming the judiciary is important, urging committee to study what best serves the public.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Argued the bill would not improve judicial independence, citing past episodes of pressure on the courts across governments.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Welcomed the aim of judicial independence but questioned clauses on conduct, business and independence from society, and suggested reworking the JSC with legal and professional members.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Said many provisions come from an earlier bill, noted court delays and space problems, and said the committee should review the clause on judges' business dealings.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the amendments, saying they give judges clearer duties and protection and that earlier governments interfered with the courts.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: As sponsor, thanked members and asked the committee to weigh their input with judges' views and prioritise speeding up delayed cases.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Presented the SOE committee report on MMPRC and the integrated tourism development company and asked the Majlis to decide on it.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Supported the SOE report and criticised opposition members for raising company debts and land allocations.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 2025/2/6 to 2025/2/8 accepted without amendment.
Asma Rasheed (Central Mafannu) assigned to the Human Rights and Gender Committee in place of Mohamed Mamdhooh.
Urgent matter from the Vaikaradhoo member declined as it did not meet the Rule 197 conditions.
Bill on seeking public opinion and holding a public vote given its first reading.
Bill to amend the Judges Act (Act 2010/13) accepted 69-0 and referred to the Judiciary Committee.
Next sitting set for Tuesday 8 July 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accepting the bill to amend the Judges Act (Act 2010/13)
